newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African wool prices rise at weekly sale.
newsitem.headline: South African wool prices rise at weekly sale.

text.p: South African wool prices rose at the latest weekly auction, the Wool Board said on Thursday.
Of the total 15,017 bales on offer, 98.2 percent was sold.
Prices for 20 micron rose 6.1 percent, 21 rose 7.7 percent, 22 rose 8.4 pct, 23 rose 8.1 percent, 24 micron rose 6.2 percent and 25 micron rose 4.8 percent.
Bellies rose 4.5 percent, lambs rose 8.9 percent and locks rose 5.1 percent.
The offering included 3,056 bales of merino together with 1,449 other white, 383 bales Ciskei, 910 bales Lesotho and 668 bales of coarse and coloured.
Top-selling wool was 23 micron which sold 100 pct.
1,022 bales offered and 99.3 percent of 20 micron sold.
1,832 bales offered and 98.1 percent of 21 micron sold.
2,734 bales offered and 98.4 percent of 22 micron sold.
676 bales offered and 97.5 percent of 24 micron were sold.
194 bales offered and 99 percent of 25 micron were sold.
The next sale will be held on January 22 with about 10,000 bales on offer.
